name: Guardian genius crossword No 278
preamble: In six of the across and seven of the down clues, a word connected to an unclued entry must be removed. All other clues contain an extra letter; these indicate a framework. Only seven other cells obey the rules of the framework and provide the keys needed for the 15ac 30ac 7d. Thanks for playing.

solutions.check: grid and clues read from the Guardian's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; each light's entry one fifteensquared prints for it, the only choice of them whose crossings all agree; an entry not its answer carries the answer as its alteration's `from`

clue.text: Audibly expressed frustration, cross about grand entrance, not so grand

indicators.note: audibly means heard, so the word is taken by its sound rather than its spelling
about can mean turned round, so the word for cross faces the other way

blocks.note: the first of the two is removed, as the preamble says: a word paired with an unclued entry
to sigh is to let out frustration in a breath
a rood is a crucifix, especially in a church

explanation.surface: Someone huffs, irritated at a showy entrance that turned out to be not so showy.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'grand' is removed: grand opera pairs with the unclued OPERA.
explanation.definitionFit: A side door is a secondary entrance, humbler than the main front door.

clue.text: Drop stage light in delivery

indicators.note: a speaker's delivery is how words are spoken, so the sound is what counts

blocks.note: removed, as the preamble says: a word paired with an unclued entry
a tier is a stage or level

explanation.surface: Stage lighting drops during a performance's delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' is removed: light opera pairs with the unclued OPERA. The answer is the crying sort, rhyming with tier.
explanation.definitionFit: A tear is a single drop of liquid from the eye.

clue.text: Shot part of Space Jam movie

indicators.note: part of a phrase is a run of letters lying within it

blocks.note: removed, as the preamble says: a word paired with an unclued entry
the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A shot from the basketball film Space Jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Space' is removed: space opera pairs with the unclued OPERA, which also breaks up the film title.
explanation.definitionFit: Shot is ammunition for guns, the pellets or bullets fired, which is ammo in casual speech.

clue.text: Meal soon returned, duck overwhelmed by sauce

indicators.note: something returned comes back the other way, so the word for son is read backwards
to be overwhelmed by something is to be engulfed by it, so these go inside

blocks.note: sauce is slang for alcohol, and vino is wine
read as son, a lad: the extra O is this clue's extra letter
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, and O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A meal arrives back soon: duck drowned in sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: Printed 'soon' is 'son' plus the extra O. The sauce is drink, not gravy: sauce is old slang for alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: A vindaloo is a hot curry, a dish eaten as a meal.

clue.text: Broken horse has minutes to find spirit

indicators.note: something broken falls to pieces, so these letters are reassembled differently

blocks.note: removed, as the preamble says: a word paired with an unclued entry
all ten letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A horse being broken in takes a few minutes to show some spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse' is removed: horse opera, a Western, pairs with the unclued OPERA, so 'Broken' no longer describes a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirit here is lively energy and eagerness, the sense of keen excitement.

clue.text: Part of system ruining life with little hesitation

indicators.note: ruining a thing wrecks its shape, so the word after it is broken up and rebuilt

blocks.note: read as lie: the F is this clue's extra letter, set aside by the preamble
um is a short hesitant noise

explanation.surface: Someone's whole way of living is being wrecked, one small pause at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'life' carries an extra F for the hidden message; the wordplay needs 'lie'. Part of system means part of the digestive system.
explanation.definitionFit: The ileum is the final section of the small intestine, one portion of the digestive tract.

clue.text: Glass less sturdy and not all there hotel admitted

indicators.note: not all of a word is used, so its last letter goes
a thing admitted is let inside, so the next word goes within the shortened one

blocks.note: removed, as the preamble says: a word paired with an unclued entry
the word with its final E cut off
an inn is a small hotel

explanation.surface: A drinking glass is flimsy, and the hotel let in a guest who was not quite all there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glass' is the word the preamble removes: it pairs with the unclued OPERA, as in opera glass, a small pair of theatre binoculars.
explanation.definitionFit: Something thinner has less bulk and substance, so it is weaker and flimsier.

clue.text: Top two in team bagging wedge for topic

indicators.note: in a down clue the top two letters of a word are its opening pair
bagging something takes it in, so the edge goes inside

blocks.note: just the first two letters
read as edge, a hem: the W is this clue's extra letter

explanation.surface: The two best players on a side bag a wedge-shaped prize for discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: Printed 'wedge' is 'edge' with the extra W. A hem is the edge of a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the subject being treated, the topic of a talk or piece of writing.

clue.text: Dish from Indiana and Arkansas served up containing first-rate bit of tenderloin

indicators.note: served up in a down clue means sent upwards, so the abbreviation is read bottom to top
containing means holding inside, so the next pieces go within
a bit of a word is a small piece of it, here just its opening letter

blocks.note: AR is the postal abbreviation for Arkansas
A1 means first-rate, written with I for one
just the opening letter

explanation.surface: A dish from the US Midwest and South, served with a prime piece of steak.
explanation.walkthrough: Printed 'Indiana' is 'Indian' plus the extra A; in Britain 'an Indian' is a curry house, so this is a dish from one.
explanation.definitionFit: Raita is a cooling yoghurt side dish served with curries in Indian cuisine.

clue.text: Frightful fellow gets paid in East London

indicators.note: the Cockney accent of East London drops an initial H, so each word loses its first letter

blocks.note: F is the standard abbreviation for fellow
gets, as in understands, is hears, said without its H
read as pad, a home, said without its H: the I is this clue's extra letter

explanation.surface: A scary character is getting his wages somewhere in the East End.
explanation.walkthrough: Printed 'paid' hides 'pad' plus the extra I. Cockneys from London's East End traditionally drop their H's, so hears and home become 'ears and 'ome.
explanation.definitionFit: Fearsome describes something that inspires dread, just as frightful does.

clue.text: Somewhere to relax essential to newspaper folk

indicators.note: essential means at the core, so the letters sit inside the word

blocks.note: removed, as the preamble says: a word paired with an unclued entry
the letters at the core of the word

explanation.surface: A place to unwind is vital for newspaper staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'folk' is removed: folk opera pairs with the unclued OPERA.
explanation.definitionFit: A spa is a resort or health centre where people go to rest and be pampered.

clue.text: 'Sugar flower had turned', Glyph put in note

indicators.note: something turned faces the other way, so the word before it is read from the end
to be put in is to be placed inside, so the setter goes within the musical note

blocks.note: removed, as the preamble says: a word paired with an unclued entry
taken as written, before being turned
the setter Glyph refers to himself as I
la is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A quoted complaint that a flower had wilted, with the setter slipping a note in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sugar' is removed, as the preamble says: sugar soap, a cleaner for paintwork, pairs with the unclued SOAP.
explanation.definitionFit: The dahlia is a showy garden bloom with many petals, a familiar flowering plant.

clue.text: Shabby looking saddle – he won't deal with repairs

indicators.note: repairs take something apart and put it back together, so these letters are reassembled

blocks.note: removed, as the preamble says: a word paired with an unclued entry
all ten letters of the phrase, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A worn saddle that its owner refuses to get mended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saddle' is removed: saddle soap pairs with the unclued SOAP, and without it the surface is a man refusing to deal with repairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Down-at-heel describes someone or something shabby and run-down, like shoes worn away at the back.

clue.text: Close to salvation, Dante frolicking around edges of hellhole - skillful!

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter
frolicking is romping about, so the letters of the name are tossed into a new order
around means encircling, so the jumbled name goes round the edges

blocks.note: just the last letter
read as date: the N is this clue's extra letter
the edges of the word are its outer letters, H and E, spelt out with the and

explanation.surface: The poet of the Inferno capers round the rim of hell as salvation nears: what dexterity!
explanation.walkthrough: Printed 'Dante' hides 'date' plus the extra N. The edges of hellhole are H and E, taken literally as H AND E.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat-handed means dexterous, deft with the hands, so skilful.

clue.text: Endlessly desired spring

indicators.note: without an end, a word loses its final letter

blocks.note: read as desire, to hope: the D is this clue's extra letter

explanation.surface: An endless longing for the season of spring.
explanation.walkthrough: Printed 'desired' is 'desire' with the extra D. Spring is the verb, to jump.
explanation.definitionFit: To hop is to spring or leap, especially on one foot.

clue.text: End relationship as one spewing about American bastard turning soft

definitions.note: read as a noun phrase, the end of a relationship

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the spewer goes round the American
turning round makes the whole assembled string face the other way

blocks.note: removed, as the preamble says: a word paired with an unclued entry
one who spews is one who pukes
A is the abbreviation for American
B is a standard abbreviation for bastard, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A sickening American scoundrel, soft-hearted after all, splits with his partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soft' is removed: soft soap pairs with the unclued SOAP. PUK(A)ER plus B, read backwards, gives BREAK-UP.
explanation.definitionFit: A break-up is the ending of a romantic partnership, a couple's separation.

clue.text: Brave peacekeepers cease supporting half of Africa

indicators.note: half of a word is one of its two halves, here the front

blocks.note: the United Nations sends peacekeeping forces
the front three of its six letters
read as ease, to aid: the C is this clue's extra letter

explanation.surface: Brave peacekeepers stop backing half a continent.
explanation.walkthrough: Printed 'cease' is 'ease' plus the extra C. In a down clue, one piece supporting another sits beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: Unafraid means without fear, so bold and courageous.

clue.text: Almost falling back, drunk inspiring doodler

indicators.note: inspiring literally means breathing in, so the drunk takes the doodle inside
falling back means going backwards, so the assembled string is read from the end

blocks.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard
read as doodle, to draw idly: the final R is this clue's extra letter

explanation.surface: A drunk, nearly toppling over, takes a breath while scribbling.
explanation.walkthrough: Printed 'doodler' hides 'doodle' plus the extra R. S(DRAW)OT is then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Towards can mean approaching or near, as in towards midnight, which is almost midnight.

clue.text: Way out in Asia, stay good at heart

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, so only central letters are kept

blocks.note: the two central letters
read as god, whose middle is O: the extra O is this clue's extra letter

explanation.surface: A traveller far off in Asia resolves to stay good inside.
explanation.walkthrough: Printed 'good' is 'god' with the extra O, and 'at heart' serves both words.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tao, in Chinese philosophy, literally means the way, the path of right living.

clue.text: Partly reduced budget – university cancelled exam relating to certain degrees

indicators.note: cancelled means struck out, so the university's letter is removed

blocks.note: read as party, a do: the L is this clue's extra letter
a cut is a reduction in a budget
U is the abbreviation for university
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A partly cut budget means the university scraps an exam for some degrees.
explanation.walkthrough: Printed 'Partly' is 'Party' with the extra L. CUT loses its U.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctoral refers to the doctorate, the highest academic qualifications such as the PhD.

clue.text: Go on! Finish off Magnums, say, with Mum

indicators.note: to finish something off here is to take off its finish, its last letter

blocks.note: read as Magnum, say: a Magnum is a powerful revolver, the S being this clue's extra letter
mum means silent, and sh is a call for silence

explanation.surface: An encouraging shout to polish off the ice lollies with your mother.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's Magnums are ice creams, but a Magnum is also a gun. Printed 'Magnums' carries the extra S.
explanation.definitionFit: To gush is to go on at length, talking effusively and without restraint.

clue.text: Flavour our Gallic friend bolsters using mushrooms initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters of the words before it

blocks.note: the first letter of each word
ami is French for friend

explanation.surface: A French friend backs a savoury taste by cooking with mushrooms.
explanation.walkthrough: Printed 'our' is 'or' with the extra U. In a down clue, AMI bolsters UM by sitting below it.
explanation.definitionFit: Umami is the savoury fifth taste, a meaty flavour found in mushrooms and broths.

clue.text: Posting amigo's corn for rural research

indicators.note: read as posing: a pose is an arranged position, so these letters are arranged afresh

blocks.note: all ten letters of the phrase, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Mailing a Spanish friend's grain off for study by country scientists.
explanation.walkthrough: Printed 'Posting' carries the extra T; the anagram signal is 'posing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Agronomics is the study of farming and land management, a branch of agricultural science.

clue.text: Get to march for Reform around centre of Bournemouth

indicators.note: a word put up for reform is to be remade, so its letters are rearranged
around means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the centre
the centre of a word is its middle letter

blocks.note: read as arch: the M is this clue's extra letter
the sixth of eleven letters

explanation.surface: Protesters reach the seaside town to march for the Reform party.
explanation.walkthrough: Printed 'march' is 'arch' plus the extra M. Bournemouth is a south-coast English resort town.
explanation.definitionFit: To reach a place is to get to it, to arrive there.

clue.text: Ballad poet's frequently using expression of wonder on paper

blocks.note: removed, as the preamble says: a word paired with an unclued entry
O! is an exclamation of awe
the FT is the Financial Times newspaper

explanation.surface: A poet often uses an exclamation of wonder on the page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ballad' is removed: ballad opera pairs with the unclued OPERA. In a down clue, O on FT puts O above.
explanation.definitionFit: Oft is an archaic, poetic form meaning often, used by poets for its single syllable.

clue.text: Aristocrat and techie both fall short finding source of hard profit

definitions.note: with the word paired with SOAP removed, the definition is source of profit

indicators.note: falling short means stopping before the end, so each of the two words loses its last letter

blocks.note: an earl is a nobleman
a nerd is an obsessive technical type

explanation.surface: A nobleman and a computer geek both miss their targets in the search for easy money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard' goes: hard soap pairs with the unclued SOAP.
explanation.definitionFit: An earner is anything that brings in money, such as a nice little earner.

clue.text: For pro-communist publicity, race US soldier first to the pole

indicators.note: the first of a word is only its opening letter

blocks.note: read as ace, A in card notation: the R is this clue's extra letter
a GI is an American soldier
just the opening letter
a pole can be a prop holding something up

explanation.surface: An American soldier racing to the North Pole for a Soviet propaganda stunt.
explanation.walkthrough: Printed 'race' hides 'ace' plus the extra R. The pole is a support, not the Arctic.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitprop is political propaganda, originally the Soviet department of agitation and propaganda.

clue.text: None admired his nude study

definitions.note: read as One admired once the extra N is set aside

indicators.note: nude means stripped bare, so the word loses its outer covering of letters

blocks.note: the word with its outer letters stripped
to con is to study or pore over

explanation.surface: Nobody thought much of the artist's nude study.
explanation.walkthrough: Printed 'None' is 'One' with the extra N, so the definition is One admired.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a revered person, someone idolised and looked up to by many.

clue.text: Comic Morgan's unfinished column

indicators.note: unfinished means lacking an end, so the name drops its final letter

blocks.note: removed, as the preamble says: a word paired with an unclued entry
Piers Morgan is a British TV presenter and former tabloid editor

explanation.surface: A funny man called Morgan leaves his newspaper column unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comic' is removed: comic opera pairs with the unclued OPERA. The column is the architectural kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A pier is a supporting pillar or column, as between arches of a bridge.

clue.text: Island chef is cooking yellow seafood

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so these letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: removed, as the preamble says: a word paired with an unclued entry
I is the abbreviation for island
the six letters of these two words, rearranged

explanation.surface: A chef on an island prepares a yellow fish dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yellow' is removed: yellow soap pairs with the unclued SOAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Icefish are fish of cold southern waters, also a name for smelt-like fish eaten as food.
